title: Sowing & planting: five-crop review
status: Second layout experiment: conventional planting only; not installed
units: Imperial, matching the current book. Exact canonical metric counterparts are retained in the source excerpts.
brief: John requested removal of clump growing from crop guides and calendar-date duplication from Sowing & planting. Keep readiness, duration and weather conditions. Clump growing will have a separate Techniques page; that page is not drafted in this experiment.

after.heading: Sow direct
after.text: Sow where the carrots will grow. Wait if the soil is cold or wet. Make shallow drills ½ in. deep and 6 in. apart, watering them first if dry. Sow very thinly; mixing the seed with dry sand can help. Cover with fine soil or compost, firm gently and keep moist while the seeds germinate.

after.heading: Thin only where needed
after.text: Leave 2–3 in. between plants. Water dry soil first, then thin in damp weather or in the evening. Firm the soil afterwards and bury or destroy the thinnings: bruised carrots attract carrot fly.

after.heading: Extend the season
after.text: Use short-rooted varieties for early or late crops. Early sowings need cloches or a sheltered spot; cover late crops with cloches.

timing_detail.heading: Extended season
timing_detail.text: Early: early Mar under cloches, or late Mar–Apr sheltered. Late: sow Aug; cover from Oct for Nov–Dec roots.

after.heading: Sow direct
after.text: Sow two seed clusters at each position, 1 in. deep and 4 in. apart, in rows 12 in. apart. Keep the seedbed moist. Soaking the clusters for several hours or overnight can help germination.

after.heading: Thin to single plants
after.text: A corky seed cluster can produce several seedlings. When they are about 1 in. high, thin to one plant at each position.

timing_detail.heading: Later sowings
timing_detail.text: Storage: late May–Jun. Early Jul can give medium roots before winter in favourable conditions.

after.heading: Sow in a nursery bed
after.text: Sow fresh seed thinly, ⅝ in. deep. This is a small bed for raising plants to move later. Waiting for suitable spring conditions reduces the risk of autumn bolting.

after.heading: Lift and transplant
after.text: Lift when the plants are about 8 in. tall and pencil-thick. Water dry ground before lifting and loosen the roots carefully. Choose strong plants; healthy roots and leaves need no trimming. Make 6 in. deep holes, 6–8 in. apart in rows 12 in. apart. Lower one plant into each hole and water in. Leave the holes to fill naturally.

after.heading: For an earlier crop
after.text: Raise individual plants in modules indoors, in bright conditions above 50°F. Harden off before planting.

timing_detail.heading: Earlier crops
timing_detail.text: Sow indoors in late winter; suitable hardened plants may go out in Apr.

after.heading: Sow under cover
after.text: For an outdoor crop, sow indoors, in pots or a seed tray of seed compost. Keep warm for germination and give seedlings plenty of light. Alternatively, buy sturdy plants of an outdoor variety and join the sequence at growing on or hardening off, according to their size.

after.heading: Prick out, then pot on
after.text: When true leaves develop, lift tray-grown seedlings into individual pots, supporting the roots and holding a leaf rather than the stem. Later, move each plant into a larger pot as its roots fill the old one. These are growing-on stages; the plants are still under cover.

after.heading: Harden off
after.text: Gradually get plants used to outdoor conditions over about two weeks. Keep them protected from frost.

after.heading: Plant out
after.text: Plant after frost risk, in settled warmth. Plants should be well rooted, with the first flowers beginning to open. Water first, keep the rootball intact and plant slightly deeper than its pot level. Space plants 18–24 in. apart, allowing more room for vigorous varieties; follow supplier guidance for compact basket types. Support tall plants and heavy bush stems, and ventilate protective cloches.

after.heading: Prepare seed potatoes
after.text: Use healthy certified seed potatoes. Chitting means letting them sprout before planting: stand them with the eyes upwards in a cool, light, frost-free place. It is most useful for first earlies.

after.heading: Plant in the ground
after.text: Early planting needs a mild or protected site. Make trenches about 6 in. deep, or use individual holes. This is the trench depth, not 6 in. of soil above each tuber. Set tubers at the base with sprouts upwards, cover gently and water well. Follow the early/maincrop spacings in Quick Facts; earth up as the stems grow to keep developing tubers covered. Protect emerging shoots from frost.

after.heading: Alternative: under mulch
after.text: Set tubers on the soil surface and cover with a thick mulch that excludes light. Keep topping it up so tubers cannot turn green, and check for slugs.

after.heading: Alternative: containers
after.text: Use a large container with drainage. Start tubers in a shallow layer of compost, cover them and add more compost as the stems grow. Keep tubers covered and water regularly.

timing_detail.heading: Preparing & planting
timing_detail.text: Chit from midwinter. Plant 1st earlies late Mar–Apr; 2nd earlies early–mid Apr; maincrops mid–late Apr, when conditions suit.
